problems.rationale: The biological arm has a plausible route through existing segmented volumes and a bounded simulation comparison, but obtaining three clean tissue types with trustworthy apical-basal topology remains uncertain. The mathematical arm requires genuinely new certified geometry or spectral analysis at foam junctions, far beyond the existing Lean facts. A logged multi-tissue scutoid test plus a rigorous restricted local-optimality certificate would move this forecast sharply upward.

approaches.note: The continuous spectral enclosure across Plateau junction lines is research-level, though a completed certificate would decisively settle restricted local stability.
A conditional Lean bound is feasible, but an unconditional three-dimensional isoperimetric development and a useful tightening are unlikely within a month.
The test is implementable if suitable segmentations can be recovered, while topology errors and cross-dataset comparability may leave the pooled verdict inconclusive.
Thirty volumes with 200 cells, high topology F1, and held-out parameterization make this substantially more data- and curation-limited than the smaller test.
Finite-dimensional restriction helps, but exact curved-interface representation and the Lean bridge to the certificate remain major obstacles.
A supplement-table audit is easy to finish, but missing numeric bins or reuse of the source paper's own predictions can make it non-independent or inconclusive.
A bounded annealing record is feasible, but only the very unlikely discovery of a lower-area foam would settle the mathematical question.
The candidate comparison is formalizable, but proving a nontrivial universal shared-face bound above the isolated-cell value is the hard promised component.

problems.rationale: Several approaches reduce to the same attainable core artifact: a carefully matched ZFIN label set, family-held-out evaluation, and a ranked untested-gene list. The main risk is not model fitting but phenotype-stage matching, allele annotation, and negative-label validity, which could shrink or bias the sample. A clean preregistered label table with adequate class counts would move the 30-day probability above one half.

approaches.note: This directly matches the acceptance criteria, with label construction and comparable stage-system phenotypes as the principal completion risk.
The fixed two-feature rule is easy to analyze, though sparse promoterless contrasts and incomplete lesion annotations may weaken the mechanistic verdict.
Morpholino sequence and rescue annotations add substantial extraction work, and residual confounding could prevent a clean attribution despite completed models.
Its stringent manual agreement, balanced sample, family holdout, temporal holdout, and calibration gates lower completion but would make the result highly decisive.
Finding fifty mutants with matched phenotype, paralogs, and public RNA-seq is doubtful, but the prespecified mediation result would directly test the mechanism.
The Boolean rule and family holdout are bounded, although zebrafish NMD annotation and anatomy-term label construction can introduce missingness.
A small leakage-resistant logistic model is operationally realistic and its failure threshold supplies a definite answer for the stated feature blocks.
The ranked list follows readily once reusable labels exist, but strict monotone decile calibration can fail from sample noise even with useful discrimination.

problems.rationale: The strongest route is a preregistered fabric-versus-stress analysis, but open whole-bone scans with independently defensible physiological loads across three sites and two species may not exist. Simulations and Lean formalizations can clarify sufficiency without meeting the biological acceptance criterion or causality arm. Successful scouting of three oriented datasets with load metadata would be the largest positive update.

approaches.note: The full FE and fabric pipeline is feasible, but licensing, anatomical orientation, and credible cross-species loads make the three-site gate uncertain.
A coarse remodelling-versus-growth simulation can be completed, though it settles model discrimination rather than real-bone causality.
The two-dimensional trigonometric mechanism is well bounded for Lean, while the Lyapunov statement over trajectories is the main formalization risk.
Reaching five independent controlled experiments with extractable rotations and dispersion is uncertain, but a qualifying meta-regression would address causality directly.
Blinded loads and stringent two-null thresholds improve decisiveness while increasing the chance that scouting or mesh convergence prevents completion.
Twenty labeled specimens and stable inverse load recovery are demanding, especially because static architecture can admit many boundary-condition explanations.
Specified repositories and explicit exclusion gates make this concrete, but the surviving oriented volumes and subject-specific load uncertainty remain limiting.
The two-dimensional bounded simulation should finish and can test sufficiency, but it cannot establish that living trabeculae remodel by the simulated rule.
The 2D symmetric-stress theorem is a tractable extension, yet it only settles the mechanics lemma rather than the empirical alignment claim.

problems.rationale: A controlled simulation can answer whether hierarchy helps in a specified model, but the problem requires a five-family, forty-record measurement-aware meta-analysis. Comparable toughness protocols and jointly reported constituent, interface, and hierarchy descriptors are likely to eliminate many records. A provenance-complete table meeting the coverage bar would substantially raise the forecast.

approaches.note: The analysis is standard once assembled, but missing interface compliance and incompatible initiation versus growth toughness threaten the required coverage.
A 2D spring sweep is tractable and decisive for its controlled model if size and lattice convergence are demonstrated.
The algebraic stiffness bounds look Lean-tractable, but they narrow rather than settle the empirical toughness question.
Protocol-aware stratification and leave-family-out prediction are strong, while obtaining forty commensurable complete records is the dominant risk.
The matched factorial design is informative, though mesh-converged cohesive failure across three nested levels may consume substantial implementation time.
Dropping every incomplete row makes the forty-record, five-family gate particularly difficult despite a straightforward regression.
Transcribing and sweeping a published recurrence is bounded and likely finishable, but it settles only that model and is sensitive to closure assumptions.
A rational counterexample to monotonicity is plausible after correct transcription, while formalizing the full recurrence without artificial scaling assumptions is uncertain.

problems.rationale: The mathematical premise can likely be clarified quickly: without buckling or radius constraints an empty tube has no interior stiffness-per-mass optimum. The biological criterion is much harder because one hundred structures across four types each require matched modulus and credible loads, which the slice explicitly identifies as sparse. A verified multi-type table with same-paper mechanical properties would be the key upward signal.

approaches.note: The empty-core monotonicity is straightforward, while the claimed unique filled-core optimum over realistic density ratios needs careful checking.
The four-type, hundred-record requirement with matched moduli and pneumaticity is the severe bottleneck, though meeting it would directly settle the criterion.
Open CT can yield geometry, but sixty licensed bones, mass range, phylogeny, and approximated load cases make the full artifact difficult and only partly germane.
The compact-feasible-set and active-constraint results are plausible, provided shell-buckling relations are explicitly assumed rather than claimed from unsupported continuum theory.
Uncertainty propagation is manageable, but matched specimen properties and loads across four structure types are unlikely to reach one hundred in a month.
The one-variable monotonicity and stationarity equations are highly bounded Lean tasks that should clarify the optimization premise.
The slice already flags absent stem compilations, blocked feather data, and missing same-paper moduli, making the exact coverage gate unlikely.
A smaller plot can probably be produced, but fewer than twenty modulus-matched points or sensitivity to the unknown buckling constant may defeat its own gate.

problems.rationale: The primary Campione data and a second mammal table appear to provide a realistic path to the required taxon count, phylogenetic regressions, and clade tests. The main uncertainty is whether the deduplicated union reaches 300 and whether an independent compilation truly replicates rather than overlaps the primary source. Safety-factor flatness needs additional force and posture data, so even a strong exponent analysis may leave that subquestion open.

approaches.note: The PGLS is routine and the primary dataset is identified, with independent coverage and a coherent reptile tree as the main uncertainties.
Clade ANCOVA is feasible on the assembled data, though sparse posture coding and small orders may limit precise heterogeneity conclusions.
The exponent identities are Lean-tractable, but the empirical safety-factor corollary is constrained by sparse effective-mechanical-advantage estimates.
The model contest directly addresses universality, with comparable independent posture data and tree-ensemble curation as its completion risks.
Matching force, posture, CT geometry, and material strength for forty species is unlikely despite the strong decisiveness of a completed analysis.
Two named open tables make completion likely, although deduplication below 300 or table disagreement could fail the acceptance bar.
The elementary exponent derivations should formalize cleanly but only establish the theoretical targets, not which law organisms follow.
The deposited lifestyle and tree data support a bounded analysis, while lifestyle remains an imperfect proxy for mechanical posture.

problems.rationale: Simulation and formalization are tractable, but the acceptance criterion hinges on independently measured modulus, swelling, diffusivity, curvature, and timing for enough specimens. The slice repeatedly warns that papers often infer swelling from curvature, creating circular inputs and likely reducing the admissible sample below twenty across five species. Discovery of a qualifying fabricated-bilayer series could provide the clearest alternate route.

approaches.note: The calculation is straightforward, but jointly independent specimen inputs and three-thickness response series are probably too sparse.
A verified FE correction map is achievable, though unmeasured interlayer and viscoelastic parameters may make biological deviations non-identifying.
The graded moment formula is formalizable, but interval integrals for step profiles and the spectral diffusion bracket create meaningful Lean risk.
Strict independent-input and leave-species-out requirements make completion unlikely but would deliver a strong test if the literature supports it.
Synthetic model recovery and an identifiability map are computationally bounded, but they design the empirical discriminator rather than supply specimens.
Named sources help, yet forbidden back-calculated swelling and inaccessible figure tables may prevent either coverage alternative from being met.
The baseline and bounded parameter sweep should complete if the solver is stable, settling the size of model deviations within that model class.
A useful explicit relative-error inequality may be algebraically difficult when curvature is near zero, and it covers only modulus uncertainty.
The required printer, humidity chamber, and operator are explicitly absent, so only an unlikely external execution can produce the decisive measurements.

problems.rationale: A thirty-shell geometry comparison is possible from images and simulations, but modern licensed micrographs, projection correction, and validated segmentation are substantive gates. The broader mineral-independence and developmental-control claims need balanced acantharian and organic examples that the slice says are not verified. A photograph-only dataset clearing the per-material sample floor would materially improve the forecast.

approaches.note: The three-null comparison is well designed, while licensed 3D-shell imagery and segmentation error relative to the null gap are uncertain.
Ten usable shells in each of silica, strontium-sulphate, and organic classes—especially Clathrulina—appears unlikely without new imaging.
The spherical simulation is feasible, but the decisive posterior comparison depends on measured shells and may find packing and tension models observationally similar.
Balanced eight-per-material calibrated images and leave-taxon-out inference make this stringent, but a completed contest would directly address both main claims.
A synthetic mechanism library can be built, though overlap or abstention is likely because mature morphology may not identify developmental mechanism.
Public drawings make thirty shells attainable, but the required photograph-subset confirmation and mineral-balanced gate may fail.
The Euler-handshaking algebra is a very small Lean proof, but it settles only a topological count under strong hypotheses.
The synthetic power check is bounded and likely finishable, although its chosen template may not span realistic cellular alternatives.

problems.rationale: The acceptance criterion is explicitly a replicated physical print-and-test experiment, while the swarm has no printer, resin, testing machine, or established operator. Simulations and design packages can be completed but cannot count as solving the printed question, so the problem probability remains below their completion-settlement products and this mismatch is intentional. A committed external facility with a scheduled blinded run would be the necessary positive update.

approaches.note: The Monte Carlo frame comparison is computationally feasible and informative for simulation, but assumed failure and defect laws limit physical decisiveness.
Files and preregistration are easy, but completion requires an absent operator to print and test sixty specimens within the month.
Eight replicated matched-mass studies may be findable, but exact strut-count matching and publication bias make the promised subset doubtful.
The large nonlinear uncertainty sweep is demanding but bounded, and it can decisively settle robust superiority only in the virtual model.
The physical artifact is highly decisive, but absent laboratory access makes completion within thirty days a long shot.
A two-dimensional ideal-strut comparison is straightforward, though it omits print defects, nonlinear failure, and the actual three-dimensional experiment.
The noise sweep should finish once meshes exist, but independent radius noise is an assumed stand-in and cannot validate a real process.
The small Lean lemma and numerical grid are tractable, but a two-bar counterexample addresses generalization rather than the printed lattice criterion.
The explicit stop before fabrication means completion depends almost entirely on unexpected external laboratory participation.
